Exemption allowed subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

1. This petition has been filed seeking quashing of FIR No.315/2019 under sections 498A/406/323/506/34 IPC PS Delhi Cantt on the ground that the parties have arrived at a settlement vide settlement /MOU dated 14th September, 2021 which is on record of this Court.
2. Petitioner nos. 1 to 3 and respondent no.2-complainant are present in the Court and have been duly identified by the Investigating Officer and their respective counsels.
3. Petitioner No. 1 and respondent No. 2 were married on 24th April, 2019 and no child was born out of wedlock.
Pursuant to the differences between themselves have now obtained the decree of divorce by mutual consent dated 25th May, 2022.

4. As per the settlement, a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- is to be paid to respondent no. 2 by the petitioner no.1 at this stage which is tendered by way of Demand Draft No.000909 dated 22nd March, 2023 drawn on AXIS Bank which she has received and acknowledged in the Court.
She further submits that she has no objection to quashing of the FIR.

5. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR Palminder Singh & Ors vs State (N.C.T Of Delhi) & Anr on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196901075/
1 as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
